primary_hypothesis: Hydrological transition dynamics can amplify or preserve differences among independently study-admissible temporal realizations sufficiently to change a preregistered event- or regime-level scientific inference.
prohibited_posthoc_actions: relocate frozen transition cases to obtain a flip
expand the failed P0B search envelope
replace the preregistered numerical floor after seeing outcomes
add convergence-tolerance variation as a rescue of the failed P0a mechanism screen
claim_ceiling: Within these preregistered B01 pilot experiments, temporal refinement changed a transition-near ponding classification without qualifying hydrological amplification, did not change the drought-stress timing class, and did not encounter the prescribed-head exchange transition inside the declared B0 envelope. This does not establish absence of amplification in vadose-zone models generally.
publication_implication: The standalone NUM-UNC paper concept is not supported by P0 in its current amplification-based form. The negative evidence may be retained as methodological or supplementary evidence elsewhere, but threshold proximity alone must not be relabelled as the intended novelty.
